questions.question: How do people collect and carry water from rivers, streams and springs?
questions.expected_answer: They walk to the river, stream or spring and fill buckets, pots or plastic containers. They carry the water home on their heads, in their arms, in wheelbarrows, in donkey carts, or with a Hippo Water Roller, which is rolled along the ground.

questions.question: Name three problems or dangers of collecting water directly from rivers and streams.
questions.expected_answer: It takes a lot of time, so children may be late for school; heavy loads can hurt necks, backs and knees; paths can be steep or unsafe and rivers can flood; the water may be dirty with germs from animals, people and rubbish, which cause diarrhoea and cholera; streams can dry up in a drought.

questions.question: Describe how to make river water safer to drink.
questions.expected_answer: Collect it from the cleanest place, upstream from animals and people washing, in clean containers. Let it stand so dirt settles, then pour off the top. Filter it through a clean cloth. Then boil it for at least one minute, or treat it with a measured amount of bleach, and store it in a clean, covered container.
